what: Every Japanese word a viewer reads or hears in Cutling's four Japanese TikTok posts (card ASG221): on-screen strings keyed to where they sit in each source, ElevenLabs voice lines with their beat, caption, hashtags, cover line, each with an English gloss. Builders render from this file.
rule: No locale is the source the others are translated from. Each Japanese line was written blind by a separate writer (a claude -p process with no tools, model opus at high effort: Fable was at its usage limit until Nov 29) given only a brief of the screen, the moment, what the line must do, its length budget, the register and Cutling's own Japanese words, never an English line. A separate cold reader (another tool-less process, told only where each string sits) read every line back into English and judged it natural or not; flagged lines went back to a fresh writer with the reader's point, or took the reader's native line, and were read again. 'written' on each line says which round it shipped from.

voice.tool: ~/Repositories/cutling-promo/tools/vo.py (its ja reading fixes: Wi-Fi as ワイファイ, iPhone as アイフォン, Mac as マック, iCloud as アイクラウド)

typography: 、 and 。 only; no ― or dash connectors. Full-width ！ and ？. A half-width space between a Latin word and Japanese (Wi-Fi は, Cutling で); none between a digit and its counter. 〜 is the range mark (火曜〜土曜). Break Japanese only where 'lines' breaks; never let a renderer wrap it on its own.

take_conditions: Run the ja takes with the simulator's language ja and region JP (-AppleLanguages (ja) -AppleLocale ja_JP), so date:M月d日 types 12月1日, the note's date types 2026/12/01, day +1d types 水曜日 and the grid counts 5,000 個のカットリング in the app's own words.

Beat 1's Messages take is the Every-app preview's iPhone ja take (seedForEveryApp, -PROMO_LANG ja, contacts from g-words.json: 中村 由美 first). g-build-status.md lists no finished iPhone ja take, so it is re-shot too.

Typing Japanese on camera: test1Note's typeText strings above are kanji and kana; the system keyboard in the take should be the Japanese one a Japanese owner has (日本語かな), and typeText must land the exact string with no conversion candidates left open. If typeText cannot, paste the line from the pasteboard in the same stretches the en take types.
